newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds drift upwards, await British budget.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds drift upwards, await British budget.

text.p: Irish bonds drifted higher in steady trade on Monday as the market awaited Tuesday's budget in Britain, dealers said.

They said yields over Germany had not changed much over the day, despite predictions from some analysts that the Italian lira's re-entry to the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) would help peripheral bond markets gain in convergence trades.

"What we saw today was steady but unspectacular progress," one dealer said. "There was steady volume -- we saw good two-way interest going through but it wouldn't be one of the better days in terms of size."
By 1630 GMT the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 25p at 102.15 to yield 5.89 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 climbed 10p to 109.10 to yield 6.59 percent.
Dealers said trade was likely to remain quiet until the UK budget was out of the way.
"British gilts had a particularly quiet day today because of the budget and the Irish market might be much the same until it's over," the dealer said.
